question.leadin: Answer the following about the early years of the American republic.
question.text: This rebellion, led by an eponymous Revolutionary War veteran in Western Massachusetts, highlighted the weaknesses of the Articles of Confederation.
question.clue: In the end, only Charles Rose and John Bly were hanged, after this event had petered out with a final conflict at Egremont.

swap.leadin: George Washington became the only US president to lead troops in combat while in office when he led the military in putting down this rebellion.
swap.text: Name this 1790s insurrection in western Pennsylvania inspired by an unpopular tax.
swap.clue: Future Treasury Secretary Albert Gallatin failed to prevent this event, an uprising that was sparked by the Report on Manufactures and Alexander Hamilton's policies.

question.leadin: This lawyer prosecuted Richard Lawrence, the attempted assassin of Andrew Jackson, and he was briefly and politely held captive on the HMS Tonnant in 1814 after negotiating with the British.
question.text: Name this man best known for a patriotic poem he wrote after he witnessed the bombardment of Fort McHenry during the War of 1812.
question.clue: This man prosecuted the would-be assassin of Andrew Jackson, Richard Lawrence, who was committed to an insane asylum for the rest of his life.

swap.text: In the early 19th century, British ships impressed American sailors into service and British forces supported Native American raids on American settlers; in Congress, War Hawks agitated until James Madison asked for the declaration of this war.
swap.clue: Northern Federalists discussed succession at the Hartford Convention during this war.

question.text: The ruling Jackson was responding to was this one, which ruled a state's law prohibiting non-Indians being on Indian land unconstitutional.
question.clue: The missionary plaintiff in this case was initially released when he claimed that he operated under federal authority as the postmaster of New Echota, but was relieved of his duties and rearrested.

swap.text: This Sauk chief led the British Band during the War of 1812 and fought a namesake war in 1832, during which his tribe was a victim of the Bad Axe Massacre.
swap.clue: A British ally in the War of 1812, this man endured a long struggle for leadership with the American-backed Keokuk before resisting an attempt to remove Native Americans from the Rock River valley in Illinois.

question.text: This battle was fought after the Treaty of Ghent was signed. The French pirate Jean Lafitte ("zhahn luh-FEET") assisted the American side led by Andrew Jackson in this battle.
question.clue: The other side fighting this battle received support from the Baratarian pirates led by Jean Laffite.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a conflict in which the U.S. participated unofficially.
swap.text: This undeclared war between the U.S. and France during the French Revolutionary Wars saw various naval clashes in the Atlantic, stemming in part from French depredations on American shipping.
swap.clue: Triumphs for that nation included the capture of the ships L'Insurgente and La Vengeance by Thomas Truxtun.

question.text: This future president used the pen name Publicola to publish a series of essays in the Columbian Centinel arguing against majority rule, which brought him into conflict in two elections against a radical democratizer.
question.clue: This defending attorney in the Amistad case sorted out border disputes and acquired Florida in a treaty signed with Spanish diplomat Luis Onis.

swap.leadin: It was publicized by Samuel Brannan, who wrote of James Marshall's find at Sutter's Mill.
swap.text: Name this event whose undertakers came to be known as the "forty-niners."
swap.clue: The oldest continuously operating Taoist temple in America was built as part of this event, during which Lola Montez moved to the town of Grass Valley.

question.leadin: Thinking of law school? If so, you might find it helpful to answer some questions about American legal precedent.
question.text: This power, granted to the Supreme Court in Marbury v. Madison, allows courts to strike down laws that judges deem unconstitutional.
question.clue: The appointment of "midnight justices" led to the case which instituted this practice.

swap.text: This "Father of Texas" organized the "Old Three Hundred," the first American families to settle in the region. He lost to Houston in the republic's first presidential election.
swap.clue: This man lost his country's first presidential election to the hero of the Battle of San Jacinto, Sam Houston.

question.leadin: Name some dudes who went to the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia.
question.text: This delegate from Massachusetts also later served as a Senator from New York. He ran on two consecutive Federalist tickets in the first decade of 1800s as Vice President.
question.clue: This person ran as a (+) Federalist in the 1816 presidential election with running mate John E. Howard but lost in a landslide to James Monroe.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Second Seminole War.
swap.text: The breaking of this 1832 agreement, an updated treaty negotiated after 1823's Treaty of Moultrie Creek, led to the Second Seminole War. Turns out not all the Seminoles were looking to move west of Mississippi within 3 years.
swap.clue: It followed the signing of a treaty at Camp Moultrie earlier in the conflict it ended.

question.text: New York Democrats who, like David Wilmot, opposed the extension of slavery to the territories, were known by this name. These opponents of the Hunkers nominated Martin van Buren for the presidency in 1848.
question.clue: In 1848 this faction of Democrats from New York joined some antislavery Whigs and members of the Liberty Party to form the Free-Soil Party.

swap.leadin: Contrary to popular belief, this man failed to achieve fully interchangeable parts while fulfilling an arms contract.
swap.text: Name this man who is more famous for an invention that may have actually been designed by Catherine Littlefield Greene. This man only fulfilled that contract for 10,000 muskets after 10 years.
swap.clue: This man allegedly met with President Adams and President-elect Jefferson, and wowed them by assembling a musket from a drawer filled with shuffled pieces that he manufactured.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Constitutional Convention.
question.text: Seconding Gerry's proposal was this man, a lawyer who later defended Samuel Chase during his impeachment trial and Aaron Burr during his treason trial, and also argued for the losing side in McCulloch v. Maryland.
question.clue: This "drunken prophet" from Maryland walked out of the Convention along with fellow state delegate John Mercer, protesting the opposition to a bill of rights. He later embraced federalism and argued on behalf of the state in McCulloch v. Maryland.

swap.text: This 1795 treaty was the first of many signed by Spain and the United States over the status of Florida. It extended the Florida/Georgia border all the way to the Mississippi River.
swap.clue: In part, it guaranteed free navigation of the Mississippi and the right of deposit in New Orleans for 3 years.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the American System.
question.text: The American System did succeed in creating this road that connected its namesake city and Vandalia. It's now known as Highway 40.

swap.text: William Marcy was succeeded as Secretary of State by this man, who also served as the second Territorial Governor of Michigan and lost to Zachary Taylor in the Election of 1848.
swap.clue: It was in that office that he directed the Black Hawk and Seminole Wars.
